primary_claim: Replicating and extending the alignment faking model organism, the authors find that open-source models (Llama, GPT-4o) show essentially no alignment faking in the prompted-only setting, but fine-tuning them on synthetic documents induces alignment faking whose rate increases disproportionately with model scale, while an improved classifier raises AF-detection AUROC from 0.62 to 0.92.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Finds Mistral Large 2 shows no AF or compliance gap, unlike recent work (LessWrong post reporting Mistral Large 2 123B exhibits alignment faking)
Original AF paper's classifier has a high false positive and negative rate, giving a poor signal on which models are showing signs of AF, though this does not change the original paper's findings
stated_future_work: Run various revealed preferences experiments to understand the motivations of models that cause AF and the compliance gap
Run experiments to understand what mechanisms make Opus and Sonnet more susceptible to AF, e.g. distilling Opus's personality into GPT-4o
Run pre-fill experiments to understand how models change their responses when we put words in their mouths
Train on synthetic documents that are precursors to AF to see if specific LessWrong posts suddenly make the model alignment fake
Look at model internals (probing and SAEs) for Llama 70B and 405B in situations where it chooses to AF
limitations_stated: We focus on the helpful-only setting, as most models are trained to refuse harmful queries while the other Claude 3 Opus preferences studied in the original paper are not widespread in other models
quote: Fine-tuning with synthetic documents disproportionately increases AF rates in larger models
